independent_adversarial_semantics_reprod.scope: standard-library disposable process and temporary-directory checks; no candidate main, formal gate, worker, model, image, or generation call

blocking_findings.title: The monitored parent is not the unique callable route to the capability-minting worker
evidence: launch_generation.py:632-650 defines spawn_bound_worker so that the function itself creates the opaque token and 256-bit secret; it does not require a parent-monitor capability from guarded_parent.
launch_generation.py:652 stores this capability minter as namespace['_spawn_capability_worker'], and line 662 returns the whole mutable namespace to its caller.
launch_generation.py:274-361 also leaves the general fork helper callable at module scope. Fixing main's public argv at lines 665-673 does not make main the only programmatic entry.

The author's own disposable self-test demonstrates that spawn_capability_worker can be called directly with a synthetic worker. It does not test calling the returned namespace['_spawn_capability_worker'] outside raw_parent.
blocking_findings.impact: After authorization, a fresh Python caller can derive the namespace and call the returned capability minter directly with the canonical paths, thereby obtaining a legitimately inherited token and entering guarded_worker without raw_parent's wall-time, RSS, disk, trace, descendant, and terminal monitoring loop. The CLI worker flag is closed, but the claimed unique monitored entry is not enforced.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Make the only exported executable entry a supervisor that establishes the attempt and monitoring state first. The worker-capability issuer must require a supervisor-only state created inside that call and must not be returned in the derived namespace or exposed as a separately callable helper. If hostile same-process callers are in scope, replace Python-object privacy with an OS-enforced parent/supervisor channel and test a fresh-interpreter direct-import attempt.

blocking_findings.title: A terminally failed prepare bundle can be promoted as the frozen core
evidence: freeze_c2_manifest.py:252-271 writes manifest_core.json before the terminal success receipt is created at lines 447-451.
On any later exception, freeze_c2_manifest.py:460-479 changes the receipt to NOT_READY_S47_C2_FREEZE_OR_ATTACHMENT_FAILED and may atomically publish that failed bundle at freeze_attempt_01.

build_attachment at freeze_c2_manifest.py:274-310 reads and validates only freeze_attempt_01/manifest_core.json; it never reads freeze_attempt_01/receipt.json, checks its status/mode, or rejects a failure receipt.
generation_gate.py:921-954 likewise binds the core file but never validates the prepare receipt or exact contents of freeze_attempt_01.
blocking_findings.impact: A normal catchable error or interrupt after manifest_core.json is written can produce an auditable failed prepare directory whose valid core is later attached and authorized. Thus prepare success is not a prerequisite for attach, and a terminal failure can silently cross the fixed prepare -> review -> attach sequence.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Before any core review or attach, require freeze_attempt_01 to be an unredirected directory containing exactly read-only manifest_core.json and receipt.json. Reconstruct and validate a success receipt with mode=prepare, status=S47_C2_CORE_FROZEN_AWAITING_TWO_REVIEWS, matching core file/core SHA, reviewed tool/protocol SHA, completed UTC, source_unchanged_at_close=true, and no failure marker. Repeat this validation in the canonical generation gate.

blocking_findings.title: SIGKILL of the sole monitor leaves the forked generation worker alive and unbounded
evidence: launch_generation.py:309-360 uses the anonymous pipe only to transmit one ordering byte and closes it immediately; no parent-liveness descriptor or watchdog remains for the scientific run.
The child calls setsid and enters worker_entry at launch_generation.py:313-331. consume_worker_capability checks os.getppid only once at lines 364-405, before raw_worker performs the long model run.

ForkWorkerProcess and every budget/descendant check live only in the parent process. There is no external supervisor capable of killing the worker process group when that parent receives uncatchable SIGKILL.
In disposable reproductions on Python 3.13.0 and 3.12.14, a forked setsid child reported after its parent exited with -9 and had been reparented to PID 1.
blocking_findings.impact: The model can continue generating after the process that enforces the 3600-second, 45-GiB, free-disk, trace, and no-survivor contract has disappeared. This can create scientific outputs without valid monitoring or an authoritative terminal parent record, while detached descendants may remain alive.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Keep a parent-liveness channel open for the full run and add an independent watchdog that kills the entire worker process group on EOF or monitor death. Publish success only through an external supervisor after it observes monitor exit 0, worker exit 0, no survivors, closed trace, and stable execution/output identities. Add SIGKILL-before-consume, SIGKILL-after-consume, SIGTERM, and late-descendant tests.

blocking_findings.title: The approved input and component bytes are reopened by pathname at scientific consumption
evidence: generation_gate.py:99-134 closes each verified descriptor after hashing. The full gate hashes C2_INPUT at line 1195 and validate_gate hashes it again at line 1284, both before the later runtime consumes the pathname.
runtime_adapter.py:195-230 proves that the S35 factory is preserved except the declared manifest, save, label, and seed edits; create_runtime invokes that derived factory at lines 253-255.

The pinned factory still loads config and component paths and finally calls load_img_and_K(m['input_image']['path'], ...) at runtime_factory.py:75,90-138. These are later opens, not consumption of the descriptors or bytes approved by the gate.

Both disposable interpreters confirmed that O_NOFOLLOW on the leaf still follows a symlink in an ancestor directory. None of the generic read_regular_snapshot helpers binds or walks every ancestor directory.
blocking_findings.impact: A path or ancestor replacement after the final hash but before a loader open can make the generated C2 row use different JPEG, YAML, weight, VAE-directory, or source bytes while the full gate and manifest retain the approved identities. The long component-loading interval makes the input hash-to-decode window material.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Carry already verified file descriptors or immutable copied snapshots into every loader, and hold verified directory descriptors for directory-based loaders. Where an API forces pathname reopening, revalidate path-to-descriptor device/inode and full content immediately before and after consumption, then bind the actually decoded input bytes and actually loaded component identities into the terminal archive. Add an ancestor-symlink and hash-then-replace negative matrix.

blocking_findings.title: Fixed attempt, authorization, and execution directories are checked by name but not held as one inode through terminal publication
evidence: freeze_c2_manifest.py:443-457 creates selected_stage and subsequently writes/publishes it entirely by pathname; no directory descriptor or stored device/inode is held. The failure handler at lines 470-481 writes no terminal record when the claimed directory has been renamed away.

create_launch_authorization.py:162-180 opens and immediately closes the attempt directory for point-in-time identity checks. After the final check at line 277 it publishes authorization and writes success_receipt.json at lines 278-293 without another attempt-identity validation.

generation_gate.py:997-1009 opens only launch_authorization_attempt_01/success_receipt.json. It does not prove the attempt path itself is an unredirected directory, bind its inode, require attempt_started.json, or require exact directory entries.

The derived S35 parent creates execution_01 by pathname and all V4 capability records use the canonical pathname without a held execution-directory descriptor. The dual disposable check confirmed that renaming a claimed fixed directory makes the canonical lease pathname immediately appear fresh again.
blocking_findings.impact: One logical attempt can be split across different directory inodes, a renamed staging lease can cease to block retry, and authorization or worker receipts can be written under a replacement ancestor after the last identity check. Fixed names alone do not establish the claimed fixed attempt or terminal evidence chain.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Hold O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW descriptors for the project parent, selected attempt, authorization attempt, execution, and output directories across their entire mutation windows. Perform all child opens/writes/renames relative to those descriptors; store device/inode identities and revalidate path-to-fd before and after each publication and before the terminal seal. Reject redirected parents and require exact terminal directory contents. Preserve a separate create-only outer attempt sentinel so renaming an inner staging directory cannot reopen the attempt.

verified_nonblocking_properties: All eight V4 candidate identities matched CANDIDATE_STATIC_SELFTEST_V4.json immediately before this review was written.

Both isolated interpreters reproduced the author's AST reversibility, seed-44 byte derivation, exact split-form CLI rejection matrix, legacy unpublished-boolean rejection, synthetic capability replay rejection, and runtime receipt temp/destination checks.
The public main argv rejects equals forms, abbreviations, repeats, alternate execution paths, unknown options, and the explicit --worker marker.
The ordinary canonical metadata and full gate routes require launch authorization; the unpublished attach preflight has a dedicated non-PASS status.
Within the output directory inode it opens, atomic_save_runtime_receipt uses a create-exclusive no-follow temp, relative dirfd operations, fsync, and a post-publication path-to-fd identity check.
The normal capability path uses a 32-byte secret plus fork-inherited object identity and rejects a second consumption in the same child state.
No V3 PASS or BLOCKED conclusion was reused as authority for V4.
